clue.text: Father with part in panto perhaps — it's a promise!

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a part played on stage, as in a pantomime, is a role

explanation.surface: Dad landing a part in the Christmas pantomime swears he'll be there.
explanation.walkthrough: Panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner released early gives a pledge of good behaviour; the word also means a solemn word of honour.

clue.text: Bearing gifts, we hear

indicators.note: says the word for gifts is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: gifts are presents

explanation.surface: Someone arrives carrying Christmas gifts, it is reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like 'carrying', but it is the definition in its sense of deportment.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bearing is their poise or demeanour, which is also called their presence.

clue.text: Resort is being rebuilt in 10 Across

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A holiday resort undergoes reconstruction during the festive merrymaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 Across is WASSAILS, here a verb meaning makes merry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs meaning celebrates noisily, carousing with drink.

clue.text: A dollop of plum pudding!

indicators.note: the dollop is taken out of the words that follow, which conceal it

explanation.surface: A spoonful of Christmas pudding being served.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum pudding is the traditional British Christmas pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless mass or chunk of something soft.

clue.text: Rates ski resorts as 'one star'

indicators.note: read as re-sorts, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: A travel guide gives a ski resort a poor one-star rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorts' looks like a noun for holiday places but is the verb re-sorts, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol * is a little star used to mark footnotes.

clue.text: Figures are cut on them by blades a foot long

definitions.text: Figures are cut on them by blades a foot long

parts.words: Figures are cut on them by blades a foot long
parts.note: skaters trace figures on ice with the blades of their skates, which are about a foot long; the surface suggests knives

explanation.surface: Something sinister: shapes slashed with foot-long knives.
explanation.walkthrough: The blades are skate blades and the figures are figure-skating patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice arenas are where skaters carve figures with their blades.

clue.text: Point the way the Wise Men came from

definitions.text: the way the Wise Men came from
definitions.meaning: the Magi were guided by a star from the Orient

explanation.definitionFit: It is a compass point, and the Magi of the Nativity came from the Orient.

clue.text: It's suspended when it is very cold at Christmas

definitions.text: It's suspended when it is very cold at Christmas

parts.words: It's suspended when it is very cold at Christmas
parts.note: a spike of frozen drips hangs from eaves in a hard winter frost

explanation.surface: Something is called off because of a Christmas cold snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspended' suggests postponed, but here it means hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapering spike of ice hangs from roofs and gutters in freezing weather.

clue.text: Touching displays of affection under the mistletoe?

definitions.text: Touching displays of affection under the mistletoe?

parts.words: Touching displays of affection under the mistletoe?
parts.note: touching means both moving and in contact with lips, as with the custom under hanging mistletoe

explanation.surface: Tender moments shared beneath the Christmas mistletoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' does double duty: heartwarming, and literally lips meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecks on the lips are the customary greeting under mistletoe.

clue.text: Game in crackers is a puzzle

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: The little game found inside Christmas crackers is a brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the Christmas novelties but is slang for mad, the anagram signal; 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or mystery that baffles is a puzzle.

clue.text: Moans about fool's revels

indicators.note: the word for moans goes around the fool, enclosing it

parts.note: to moan is to wail
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a buffoon's merrymaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To go wassailing is to make merry with drink at Christmas, an old word for festive carousing.

clue.text: Revises match arranged for today

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A sports fixture is rescheduled for today.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 24 December, so 'today' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The puzzle was published on 24 December, the day before the festival.

clue.text: Takes down what is on the Christmas menu

definitions.meaning: to take food down is to swallow or consume it

definitions.text: what is on the Christmas menu
definitions.meaning: food, as a plural noun in slang

explanation.surface: Someone copies down the dishes on the festive menu.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means consumes; as a plural slang noun it means food.

clue.text: Paper decoration coming from China

indicators.note: the letters come out of the given word in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Paper decorations imported from China.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper chains of linked loops are a classic homemade Christmas decoration.

clue.text: Ice in the drink

parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea; a sheet of ice floats there

explanation.surface: Ice cubes in a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is informal for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating sheet of sea ice is found in the ocean, slangily the drink.

clue.text: Distribute the whole first part of the Bible

parts.note: the whole is all of it
OT is the Old Testament, the first part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Hand out the entire opening section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate shares is to distribute or apportion them.

clue.text: Article being cut out of yearbook creates void

indicators.note: the article is removed from the word for yearbook

parts.note: an annual is a yearbook, such as a Christmas children's annual
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Censoring an article leaves a gap in the yearbook.
explanation.definitionFit: To void a contract or marriage is to cancel it legally, to declare it invalid.

clue.text: Waits to do it!

parts.note: waits were bands of street musicians who sang hymns door to door at Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone lingers, ready to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waits' is not the verb but an old British word for Christmas street singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Going door to door with festive songs is exactly what the waits did.

clue.text: Time for a mass celebration?

parts.note: ... Mass is celebrated at twelve on Christmas Eve; mass suggests a crowd

explanation.surface: When is the big party?
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass celebration' reads as a crowd's party, but it is the church's Christmas service.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock at night is when the Christmas Mass is held.

clue.text: Start off Happy New Year in fancy dress — no special venue

indicators.note: dressed up in a new guise, so the letters are rearranged
only the start of the following word is taken off and used

explanation.surface: A costume party to begin the New Year, location unspecified.
explanation.definitionFit: Any place at all means no particular location is required.

clue.text: Gift of new tunic to Robin

indicators.note: the letters are made new by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A present of new clothing for Robin.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation or offering given is a gift.

clue.text: Pessimistic doctor cooked bird

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy medic roasted the Christmas bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloomy outlook dwells on dark, unhealthy thoughts.

clue.text: Pub's bill for wine

parts.note: a bar is a pub; with the 's it gives an s
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: The pub's tab for the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux, named after its village.

clue.text: Forget start of carol, being confused, it's not written down

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order
the opening letter of the word for a song is forgotten

explanation.surface: A muddled singer forgets how a carol begins and has no lyric sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter of carol leaves AROL, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test or statement is verbal, not written.

clue.text: Prepares gifts, say, and lots of cards

explanation.surface: Wrapping presents and lots of Christmas cards.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means wraps up for sending; as a noun, sets of playing cards.

clue.text: Small present that may arrive around Christmas time

definitions.text: that may arrive around Christmas time

parts.note: the present moment is now

explanation.surface: A little gift that might come at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests a gift but means the present time.
explanation.definitionFit: A white Christmas comes with wintry flakes falling.

clue.text: Tree that's inspected by a fortune-teller

definitions.meaning: a palmist reads the inside of the hand

explanation.definitionFit: It is a tree with large fronds and the inner surface of the hand read by palmists.

clue.text: She joins Jack climbing nursery slopes

definitions.text: She joins Jack climbing nursery slopes

parts.words: She joins Jack climbing nursery slopes
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Jack and his companion went up the hill to fetch water

explanation.surface: A woman accompanies Jack on the beginner ski runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery slopes' suggests beginner skiing, but means the hill of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl who went up the hill with Jack in the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: Steadily as Christmas guests might once have travelled

definitions.text: as Christmas guests might once have travelled
definitions.meaning: by stagecoach, as on old Christmas cards

explanation.surface: Visitors arriving slowly, as they did in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: It means gradually, and also travelling by stagecoach as visitors once did.

clue.text: Commercial song that one often hears with bells

definitions.text: that one often hears with bells
definitions.meaning: the carol title pairs the word with bells

explanation.surface: An advertising tune heard with sleigh bells.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an advertising ditty and the first word of the song before 'Bells'.

clue.text: Part of year that includes the present time

definitions.text: Part of year that includes the present time

parts.words: Part of year that includes the present time
parts.note: the month containing Christmas, the time for presents, and the time of publication

explanation.surface: A period of the calendar that covers right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present time' means both now and the season of gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth month holds Christmas, when presents are given.

clue.text: Spirit of Noel follows this?

parts.note: Noel Coward wrote the comedy ... Spirit, so Spirit follows this word in his title

explanation.surface: Christmas cheer comes after this.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel is the playwright Noel Coward, not Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward's ghost comedy title puts this cheerful word before 'Spirit'.
